title: Component Sunset & Back-Compatibility Playbook for Tokens, Controls, and Data Visuals
creator: Aisha Kaur
summary: Create a pragmatic, developer- and product-friendly playbook for sunsetting UI tokens and components (buttons, tables, charts) while guaranteeing backward compatibility paths, automated migration hints, and a clear RFC + review checklist flow.
background: As our component library expands and we introduce more opinionated tokens and accessibility improvements, we need a predictable way to retire older tokens and component variants without breaking downstream apps. Existing docs are scattered: design tokens guidance exists, component evolution notes exist, but we lack an operational playbook that ties RFCs, automated codemods, design reviews, runtime feature flags, and support SLAs together.
goals: Define a repeatable lifecycle (Proposal -> RFC -> Implementation -> Migration -> Sunset) for tokens and components
Provide a concrete review checklist that includes API stability, accessibility regression tests, perf implications, and telemetry needs
Specify automated tooling: codemods, lint rules, and console deprecation banners for customers
Document expected timelines and responsibilities across Design, Eng, and PM for each deprecation
Ship sample migration guides for token renames and table/chart prop consolidations
out_of_scope: Large-scale component rewrites that require re-architecture of runtime (these become separate ENG initiatives)
Policy for open-source third-party forks (this playbook is internal-first)
Billing or SLA revocation policy for Dedicated/Private customers
acceptance_criteria: A publicly accessible playbook doc in Confluence with version history and owner fields
A lightweight RFC template extension for deprecation proposals (contains migration plan, telemetry hooks, fallback behavior)
A review checklist (Design/Eng/PM/Security) added to PR templates and design reviews
Two example codemods (token rename, prop consolidation) committed to monorepo and CI-validated
A console banner prototype that surfaces upcoming deprecations to customers with a link to migration notes
milestones_and_timeline: Week 1-2: Draft playbook + RFC template (Design lead: Aisha)
Week 3: Internal walkthrough with Eng + PM, collect feedback
Week 4: Implement review checklist and PR template changes
Week 5-6: Build example codemods + CI integration (Eng: Daniel Chu)
Week 7: Console banner prototype + E2E smoke (Frontend: Lina Park)
Week 8: Publish doc, announce deprecation playbook to internal teams and partners
review_checklist: API compatibility: confirm props/attributes are additive or provide explicit migration mapping
Tokens: ensure token alias mapping exists and cross-references fallback values
Accessibility: results of automated A11y scan and manual keyboard/voice review
Performance: microbenchmarks for charts/tables with large datasets
Telemetry: events to track adoption and errors after ship
Docs: migration guide, code examples, changelog entry, FAQs
Rollout plan: feature flag gating, canary percentage, and rollback plan
Security: confirm no new sensitive data exfiltration in telemetry
migration_examples: Token rename: spacing.xs -> space-2 with codemod and token alias shim for 6 months
Button variant removal: primaryAlt -> primary-v2; provide CSS shim and prop mapping with runtime warning in dev builds
Table prop consolidation: `rowSelection` and `selectedRows` consolidated into `selection` with clear mapping and eslint rule to auto-fix
Chart axis API change: expose new axis object while keeping old axis* props with deprecation console warnings
codemod_plan: Scope codemod for each change and publish as a CLI under internal/batch-migrations
Add lint rule that errors on old tokens when migration window closes
Run codemod on top 30 active repos, surface failures in a migration dashboard
Provide `--dry-run` output and PR templates that can be auto-created by the migration bot
decision_log: 2025-11-12: Agreed that deprecation windows default to 180 days for internal-only changes and 270 days for public API changes (Design + PM + Eng)
2025-12-03: Decided to use console deprecation banners plus opt-in telemetry rather than email-first approach
2026-01-15: Chose to require an RFC for any change that touches tokens consumed by >5 services (threshold configurable)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large surface area changes may break partner integrations. Mitigation: partner pre-release program and extended migration windows.
Risk: Teams may ignore migration. Mitigation: automated codemods, lint rules, and periodic migration sprints supported by engineering hours.
Risk: Incomplete migration docs. Mitigation: require migration guide as part of PR gating and add reviewers from owning teams.
